headline: High-risk default interaction: AutoGPT can write and browse files while Rasa ingests external chat channels, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs; Rasa ingests messages from Slack, Telegram, Twilio, and similar channels. If AutoGPT outputs land in a shared file or message path, Rasa may treat attacker-controlled content as conversational input. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes instructions into a shared file or channel that Rasa reads
IF Rasa is configured to consume untrusted upstream text without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable any shared file or queue bridge
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent messages
Require human review before Rasa consumes AutoGPT output
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and execute shell commands, while Rasa handles text and voice from external messaging surfaces. If either agent is pointed at the same workspace or transcript store, sensitive content can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs. No profile field shows isolation or encryption controls, so the safe assumption is shared-data exposure is possible.
conditions: IF both agents read from the same directory or transcript store
IF sensitive chat transcripts are exported into files AutoGPT can access
mitigations: Use separate storage locations per agent
Restrict AutoGPT to a non-sensitive sandbox directory
Rotate or redact transcripts before file ingestion
Audit shared mounts and API logs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT has shell and subprocess execution plus filesystem access; Rasa exposes external messaging integrations and processes dialogue. Both profiles indicate no multiple-instance support, so concurrent writes or state updates can collide if they share a workspace, config, or deployment target. The conflict is plausible without any locking mechanism being documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or config file
IF either agent is deployed with shared mutable state and no lock
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Back up shared state before runs
Check for lockfile support in deployment
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate arbitrary text and act via shell/subprocesses, while Rasa is a dialogue system that can surface or route that text through chat channels. If Rasa treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, downstream actions or replies can propagate errors without verification. Because the pair lacks documented validation boundaries, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Rasa forwards AutoGPT-generated text to users or tools without verification
IF AutoGPT output is used as a source of facts or commands
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before actioning outputs
Require schema validation on AutoGPT outputs
Limit Rasa to templated responses only
Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGPT is a general filesystem-and-shell agent, while Rasa processes text and voice across third-party messaging integrations. The profiles do not document residency, retention, or certification alignment, so compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is routed through the pair. Uncertainty pushes this above low because the data path is broad and externally connected.
conditions: IF regulated customer data or transcripts are routed through both agents
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Block regulated data from AutoGPT workspaces
Review retention settings on all chat connectors
Document residency for each integration
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and contractual terms
